info.description:
## Overview

Use this API specification, as a secondary care provider, to build an API that the Wayfinder Direct Integration service can use to manage appointments for a patient using FHIR R4 (4.0.1).

This specification contains the following operations:
* Search for appointments, including supported `_include` results.
* Get, create, update, patch and delete an appointment.
* Retrieve the server capability statement using `/metadata`.

FHIR APIs are RESTful APIs that follow specific rules. In particular:
* resource names are capitalised and singular, for example `/Appointment` not `/appointments`
* array names are singular, for example `entry` not `entries` for FHIR bundle entries
* data items that are country-specific and thus not included in the FHIR global base resources are usually wrapped in an `extension` object

## Relationship to BaRS

This Direct Integration API is based on and aligned with the Booking and Referral Standard (BaRS). It focuses on the Appointment and metadata operations described in this specification.

BaRS is the definitive reference for the standard, including its requirements, resource definitions and implementation guidance. This specification supplements that guidance for direct integration; it does not replace or redefine BaRS. If this specification differs from BaRS, the BaRS standard takes precedence, and the difference should be treated as a limitation to be resolved.

Refer to the [BaRS implementation guide](https://simplifier.net/guide/nhsbookingandreferralstandard) for the authoritative guidance. Alignment with BaRS does not, by itself, establish that this specification has been formally assessed or approved as conformant.

## Who can use this API standard

You can only use this API standard if you are integrating a secondary care booking system with the Wayfinder Direct Integration service.

As a secondary care provider, you will also need to use the [Patient Care Aggregator Record Service API](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/api-catalogue/patient-care-aggregator-record-service/patient-care-aggregator-record-service-api) to let the Patient Care Aggregator know which patients you have appointments for.

## Status

This API specification is in **draft / experimental** status. It is available for review and prototyping and might be subject to breaking changes. The server CapabilityStatement returned by `/metadata` reports `status: draft` and `experimental: true`.

## Technology

This API standard is [RESTful](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/api-technologies-at-nhs-digital#basic-rest). It conforms to the [FHIR](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/api-technologies-at-nhs-digital#fhir) global standard for health care data exchange, specifically to [FHIR R4 (v4.0.1)](https://hl7.org/fhir/r4/). It includes some country-specific FHIR extensions, which have been built against [FHIR UK Core](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/fhir-uk-core).

## Network access

This API is available on the internet and, indirectly, on the [Health and Social Care Network (HSCN)](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/health-and-social-care-network). For more details, see [Network access for APIs](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/network-access-for-apis).

## Non-functional requirements

Your API must be a gold service, meaning it is operational and supported 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. For more details, see [service levels](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/reference-guide#service-levels).

Your endpoint must be capable of:
* responding to requests within 400ms (at the 95th percentile)
* a throughput of at least 60 transactions per second

Diagnostic logging requirements:
* all requests must be logged for diagnostic purposes
* log records must include the `X-Correlation-Id`
* personally identifiable and clinical information must be omitted from logs in production
* log records must be held for a minimum of 90 days

## Security and authentication

This prototype supports two alternative authentication modes on every operation, including `/metadata`: patient-based, user-restricted access through NHS login and NHS API Platform token exchange; or application-based, application-restricted access through NHS API Platform client credentials with a signed JWT client assertion. Supply one API Platform bearer access token for the selected mode. Applications must be onboarded and authorised for that mode. This is the prototype's security profile; BaRS remains the definitive reference for the underlying standard.

### Patient-based authentication flow

Register the application separately with NHS login and NHS API Platform and enable access to this API in the chosen environment.

1. Authenticate the patient using the NHS login OpenID Connect authorisation-code flow and validate the returned ID token.
2. Exchange that ID token at the NHS API Platform token endpoint, authenticating the application with a signed client assertion.
3. Send the resulting API Platform access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every API request, including `/metadata`.

Use `https://int.api.service.nhs.uk/oauth2/token` for integration testing and `https://api.service.nhs.uk/oauth2/token` for production. Follow the [NHS token-exchange guidance](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/security-and-authorisation/user-restricted-restful-apis-nhs-login-separate-authentication-and-authorisation) for request parameters, client assertions, token refresh and environment pairing.

The bearer credential for this API is the exchanged access token. Do not send an NHS login ID token, NHS login access token or client assertion as this API's bearer credential.

### Patient identity and verification

NHS login uses `openid` for authentication; request the approved `profile` scope when an NHS number is needed for patient matching. Validate identity claims and the returned verification level using the [NHS login OIDC guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/oidc-login-flow/) and [scopes and claims guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/scopes-and-claims/).

Prototype policy: patient-based appointment access requires high identity verification (P9). Configure the accepted authentication vectors during onboarding; do not infer adequate assurance merely from a successful sign-in. See [NHS login verification guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/step-up-p5-p9/).

### Application-based authentication flow

Register the application and its public key with NHS API Platform and enable application-restricted access to this API in the chosen environment.

1. Generate a signed JWT client assertion using the application's private key.
2. POST to the environment's token endpoint using `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, with `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer` and `client_assertion=<signed application client assertion>`.
3. Send the returned access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on each API request, including `/metadata`.

Use the integration or production token URL given above. Follow the [NHS application-restricted authentication guidance](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/security-and-authorisation/application-restricted-restful-apis-signed-jwt-authentication) for signing requirements and token renewal. This mode does not authenticate a patient through NHS login; the patient P9 requirement does not apply to application credentials.

### Token validation and authentication context

The API gateway must validate the API Platform access token, its authorisation for this API and its authentication mode. It must convey the authenticated application, mode and, for patient-based access, patient identity and assurance to the receiving service through a trusted channel. The receiving service must reject untrusted identity context. Do not assume an access token is a locally decodable JWT. Never select application-based access merely because patient identity is missing or an organisation header is present; reject incomplete or invalid authentication context.

### Organisation header

`NHSD-End-User-Organisation` is optional in the OpenAPI parameter definition because its requirement depends on the authenticated mode. It MUST be provided for application-based authentication and SHOULD NOT be provided for patient-based authentication, including requests to `/metadata`. For application access, the receiving service must validate the decoded organisation identifier against the organisations the authenticated application is permitted to represent. Supplying this header does not itself establish authority. For patient access, its presence must not change the authentication mode or broaden access.

### Patient authorisation — prototype policy

For patient-based access, every appointment request must be authorised against the authenticated patient's local record:

* Searches return only that patient's appointments. Supplied identifiers and demographic filters must not broaden access to another patient.
* Reads, updates, patches and deletes require the appointment to belong to that patient.
* Creation must bind the appointment to that patient. Updates and patches must not reassign it to another patient.
* Included resources must be authorised for disclosure in the context of the permitted appointment.
* Acting for another patient requires a separately defined delegated-access policy; this prototype does not grant that access.

Authentication does not automatically permit every operation. The receiving service must also enforce its appointment-management rules and application permissions. Routing, software, organisation and practitioner headers provide context, not proof of patient identity.

### Application authorisation — prototype policy

For application-based access, the receiving service must authorise each operation against the authenticated application's permissions, validated organisation context and the requested patient and appointment. Application authentication does not grant unrestricted access to all patients.

* Searches and included resources must be restricted to records the application and represented organisation are authorised to access. Patient identifiers and demographic filters select records; they do not prove authority to access them.
* Reads, updates, patches and deletes require permission for the target appointment and patient.
* Creation requires permission to create an appointment for the specified patient. Updates and patches must not bypass patient or organisation access restrictions.
* Enforce appointment-management rules and record the authenticated application and validated organisation in the audit trail. Any supplied practitioner context must be checked against the receiving service's policy and does not itself authenticate a practitioner.

### Authentication and authorisation failures

Return `401` for missing, invalid or expired API credentials, with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge. Return `403` when valid credentials lack sufficient permissions, organisation or patient access, or required patient assurance. Return an OperationOutcome without disclosing another patient's details. For application-based requests, return `400` with an OperationOutcome when the required organisation header is missing or malformed, and `403` when the application is not permitted to represent the supplied organisation. OAuth token-endpoint errors follow the linked NHS guidance and are outside this API's paths.

### Deployment

This specification defines the intended security contract. API Platform configuration for both modes, token validation, organisation validation and mode-specific authorisation must be implemented and enabled before deployment. NHS login onboarding and patient identity verification are additionally required for patient-based access. Listing the NHS API Platform environment URLs does not imply that this API is already available on NHS API Platform.

## Errors

Error responses use HTTP status codes and the OperationOutcome structure defined in this specification.

get.description:
### Returns bookings for a specified patient
Use this endpoint to get all bookings for a given patient. All bookings for the specified patient at the specified target endpoint will be returned in a FHIR searchset Bundle containing Appointment resources. 

If a sender wants to cancel a particular booking, they must perform a read first, comparing and amending the details prior to performing the update.

Patient access: the receiving service must authorise this operation for the authenticated patient and restrict all returned or modified resources accordingly. See the patient-authorisation policy in the API overview.

Application access: the receiving service must authorise this operation for the authenticated application and validated organisation. Appointment and included-resource access must be limited to permitted records. NHSD-End-User-Organisation MUST be supplied. See the application-authorisation policy in the API overview.

BookingsForPatient.description: A default response, with no `_include` parameters supplied, containing only the matched Appointment resources.

BookingsForPatientWithIncludes.summary: Get bookings for a patient, with _include=Appointment:slot&_include=Slot:schedule&_include=Schedule:actor:HealthcareService&_include=HealthcareService:location
BookingsForPatientWithIncludes.description:
A response to a request such as:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:slot&_include=Slot:schedule&_include=Schedule:actor:HealthcareService&_include=HealthcareService:location`

The matched Appointment is returned with `search.mode: "match"`, and each additionally requested resource (Slot, Schedule, HealthcareService and Location) is returned alongside it in the same Bundle with `search.mode: "include"`, so the sender does not need to make separate follow-up reads to resolve them.

AppointmentInclude_QParam.name: _include
AppointmentInclude_QParam.description:
Inclusions that drive the recursive depth of the search. Use this to ask the Receiver to return additional resources referenced by the Appointment(s), in the same response Bundle, rather than the sender having to perform separate follow-up reads.

**Note**: _include shares the same syntax as _revinclude - up to three components, separated by colon characters (:). Unlike search queries, this is not a FHIRPath expression.

The parameter can be repeated to request more than one inclusion on the same request, allowing a full chain of related resources (for example Appointment -> Slot -> Schedule -> HealthcareService -> Location) to be resolved in a single call.

The full list of applicable _includes are shown below. If any cannot be honoured the Receiver will respond, ignoring the unsupported _include(s), with the url reflecting this omission in the response Bundle.link.url.

|Expression                        | Inclusion         |Description|
|-------                           |--------           |-------- |
| Appointment:slot                 | Slot               | Include the Slot Resource(s) referenced within the Appointment Resources|
| Appointment:based-on             | ServiceRequest     | Include the ServiceRequest (referral) Resource that the Appointment is based on|
| Slot:schedule                    | Schedule           | Include Schedule Resources referenced within the Slot Resources|
| Schedule:actor:Practitioner      | Practitioner       | Include Practitioner Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| Schedule:actor:PractitionerRole  | PractitionerRole   | Include PractitionerRole Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| Schedule:actor:HealthcareService | HealthcareService  | Include HealthcareService Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| HealthcareService:providedBy     | Organization       | Include Organization Resources referenced within the HealthcareService Resources|
| HealthcareService:location       | Location           | Include Location Resources referenced within the HealthcareService Resources|

**Example usage**

Get bookings for a patient and include just the Slot each booking is linked to:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:slot`

Get bookings for a patient and resolve the chain from Slot through to the HealthcareService and Location it is delivered at:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:slot&_include=Slot:schedule&_include=Schedule:actor:HealthcareService&_include=HealthcareService:location`

Get bookings for a patient and include the referral (ServiceRequest) each booking was based on:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:based-on`

AppointmentIncludeIterate_QParam.name: _include:iterate
AppointmentIncludeIterate_QParam.description: Requests an additional resource by following a reference from a resource already returned through `_include`. For example, when a PractitionerRole is included, use `PractitionerRole:practitioner` to include its referenced Practitioner in the same search Bundle. This parameter is optional and can be repeated when more than one iterative inclusion is supported.

Below are examples of potential HTTP status codes and their associated error codes, which could be returned in the event of a fault. 

| HTTP status | Error code                 | Description |
| ----------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 400         | SEND_BAD_REQUEST           | The API was unable to process the request. |
| 400         | REC_BAD_REQUEST            | The Receiver has responded stating the message was malformed. |
| 401         | SEND_UNAUTHORIZED          | The API deemed you unauthorized to make this request. |
| 401         | REC_UNAUTHORIZED           | The receiver deemed you unauthorized to make request. |
| 403         | SEND_FORBIDDEN             | Missing or Expired Token. |
| 404         | PROXY_NOT_FOUND            | No related people exist for given NHS number. |
| 404         | REC_NOT_FOUND              | Patient record for given NHS number has been invalidated and not superseded by another NHS number. |
| 405         | SEND_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED    | HTTP Verb is not correct for this scenario.|
| 405         | REC_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED     | Receiver does not allow this.|
| 405         | PROXY_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED   | Proxy does not allow this.|
| 406         | SEND_NOT_ACCEPTABLE        | Senders message had an incorrect content type defined for a response.|
| 408         | REC_TIMEOUT                | The downstream domain processing has not completed within the configured timeout period. |
| 409         | SEND_CONFLICT              |  |
| 409         | REC_CONFLICT               |  |
| 409         | PROXY_CONFLICT             |  |
| 422         | SEND_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY  | Message was not malformed but deemed unprocessable. |
| 422         | REC_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY   | Message was not malformed but deemed unprocessable. |         
| 422         | PROXY_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY | Message was not malformed but deemed unprocessable. |         
| 429         | SEND_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS     | The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time|
| 429         | REC_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS      | The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time|

RequestingOrganisation.title: NHSD-End-User-Organisation
RequestingOrganisation.description:
Requesting Organization described in an object based on a FHIR 'Organization' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).
This header is optional in the API definition because its use depends on the authentication mode. It MUST be provided for application-based authentication and SHOULD NOT be provided for patient-based authentication. It does not identify the patient and must not be used to establish patient authorisation.

In this example an ODS code and the Organisation name is provided. Other identifiers are permitted if required.

RequestingPractitioner.title: NHSD-Requesting-Practitioner
RequestingPractitioner.description:
Requesting Practitioner described in an object based on a FHIR 'PractitionerRole' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).

This item is not mandatory, however if the information is available it must be included in the request. Only in the event that it is not available, should it be omitted.

The example below shows a General Practitioner and their SDS Role profile Id.
The Base64 encoded example below shows a General Practitioner and their SDS Role profile Id.

RequestingSoftware.title: NHSD-Requesting-software
RequestingSoftware.description:
Requesting Software described in an object based on a FHIR 'Device' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).
Access-control requirements for these headers depend on the receiving implementation. 

The identifier used here, though arbitrary, should be consistent across instances of a product, the name and version of the product should also be accurate and consistent.

NHSLoginPatientAccess.description: NHS API Platform access token obtained after NHS login authentication and token exchange. Accepted on all operations as an alternative to NHSApplicationAccess; patient-level authorisation applies. See Security and authentication in the API overview. OpenAPI 3.0 has no native token-exchange flow, so this scheme describes the bearer credential presented to this API.

NHSApplicationAccess.description: NHS API Platform access token obtained using OAuth 2.0 client credentials with a signed JWT client assertion. Accepted on all operations as an alternative to NHSLoginPatientAccess. NHSD-End-User-Organisation MUST be supplied and validated against the authenticated application. Application and organisation permissions apply. This scheme describes the bearer credential sent to the API; acquire the token using the documented signed-assertion flow.
